purpose: Tobramycin is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, especially those caused by a type of bacteria called Pseudomonas. It is commonly used for lung infections in people with cystic fibrosis, as well as eye infections. It works best against certain hard-to-treat bacterial infections that other antibiotics may not handle well.
how_it_works: Tobramycin works by entering bacterial cells and interfering with their ability to make proteins they need to survive and grow. Without these proteins, the bacteria cannot function properly and eventually die off. Think of it like pulling out a key part of the bacteria's machinery so it stops working and your body can clear the infection.
common_side_effects: When inhaled, it may cause cough, throat irritation, hoarseness, or a change in your voice. Eye drops may cause mild stinging, redness, or blurred vision right after using them. If given by injection, you may experience nausea, rash, or injection site discomfort.
warnings: Tobramycin can affect your kidneys and hearing, especially if used for a long time or at high doses, so your doctor may check your kidney function and hearing during treatment. Tell your doctor right away if you notice ringing in your ears, dizziness, or decreased urination. Let your doctor know about all other medications you take, because some drugs combined with tobramycin can increase the risk of kidney or hearing problems.
typical_dosing: For lung infections in cystic fibrosis, the inhaled form is usually taken twice a day for 28 days, then you take a 28-day break before repeating. Eye drops are typically applied one to two drops into the affected eye every 4 to 6 hours. If given by IV or injection in a hospital, dosing is carefully calculated by your medical team based on your weight and kidney function.
